leads.name: The Gerichtslinde of Erdmannrode

location.address: An der Steingasse, near the church, Erdmannrode, 36269 Schenklengsfeld, Hessen, Germany

leads.access: Free. Stands on an octagonal sandstone-walled meadow beside the church, open village ground.
leads.transport: In the village of Erdmannrode, part of Schenklengsfeld, Hersfeld-Rotenburg district, Hessen; reached by road.
leads.verify_notes: Single-tree-destination candidate (2026-08-31 exception): a summer linden roughly 500 years old with a huge girth of 8.65m (baumkunde.de, measured 1 Feb 2024 at 30cm height), height 20.0m, vital with age-appropriate damage, new shoots and callus growth. Officially a designated Naturdenkmal, confirmed by its own entry in de.wikipedia's Liste der Naturdenkmale in Schenklengsfeld (coordinates 50.81187N 9.78673E, near-exact match to baumkunde's own coordinate). Documented as an old Gerichtslinde (court linden) and counted among the region's 'geleitete Linden' (guided/trained lindens), the same recognised regional folk-tree type as the already-published Schwalm-Eder-Linden cluster (data/research/schwalm-eder-linden-verified.json, sel_001-sel_004), though this tree sits 33.5km from that cluster per the earlier check in _famous-germany.json's note and so stands on its own rather than joining it. Until around 1900 it reportedly carried a musicians' platform. The trunk is two-stemmed with wooden supports, the classic pattern of an old hollow linden's stem splitting and re-stabilising. Two independent sources agree on species, location and Naturdenkmal status; only baumkunde carries the size figures, so age and girth rest on one measurement, flagged accordingly. Anecdote to lead with: an 8.65m-girth court linden that once carried musicians on a platform in its own branches.
